newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia police arrest, beat demonstrators-opposition.
newsitem.headline: Serbia police arrest, beat demonstrators-opposition.

text.p: Police arrested three anti-government demonstrators and beat two of them in the Serbian town of Smederevo on Sunday, the opposition group Zajedno (Together) said in a statement.
Zajedno said the protesters were seized after jeering at groups of citizens who had assembled in the town to demonstrate their support for Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.

A wave of protests and counter-protests in Serbia kicked off 35-days ago after Milosevic's ruling SPS party managed to overturn opposition victories in key municipal elections, including those for the capital, Belgrade.
At least one international news organisation with representatives on the spot confirmed two protestors had been arrested in Smederevo but could not verify the reported beatings.

Several hundred Milosevic supporters gathered in Smederevo, 40 km (25 miles) south of Belgrade, for a pro-government demonstration staged to help counter the wave of anti-Milosevic protests by Zajedno.
Hundreds of Zajedno supporters gathered in the town at the same time.
Police blocked some news photographers and television crews from recording Sunday's arrests.
A huge pro-government rally is planned for Tuesday in Belgrade, where students and Zajedno supporters in their tens and sometime hundreds of thousands have clogged the streets for more than a month.
Zajedno has accused the security forces of stepping up intimidation of its supporters, saying more than 30 people have been arrested so far in demonstrations.
